## Proof

We wish to count the zeros of $g(z) := f(z) - z$ in the open unit disc $|z| < 1$.

**Setup.** Since $f$ is analytic on $|z| \le 1$ and $|f(z)| < 1$ for $|z| \le 1$, the function $g(z) = f(z) - z$ is analytic on a neighborhood of the closed unit disc.

**No zeros on the boundary.** Suppose $g(z_0) = 0$ for some $|z_0| = 1$. Then $f(z_0) = z_0$, giving $|f(z_0)| = |z_0| = 1$, which contradicts the hypothesis $|f(z)| < 1$ for $|z| \le 1$. Hence $g$ has no zeros on $|z| = 1$, so the number of zeros inside is well-defined and finite.

**Applying Rouché's Theorem.** On the boundary $|z| = 1$ we have
$$|f(z)| < 1 = |z| = |-z|.$$
Set $F(z) = f(z)$ and $G(z) = -z$. Then $|F(z)| < |G(z)|$ holds strictly on $|z| = 1$. By Rouché's Theorem, $F + G$ and $G$ have the same number of zeros (counted with multiplicity) inside $|z| < 1$:
$$N(F + G) = N(G).$$
Here $F + G = f(z) - z = g(z)$, and $G(z) = -z$ has exactly one zero (at $z = 0$, of multiplicity one) inside $|z| < 1$.

**Conclusion.** Therefore $g(z) = f(z) - z$ has exactly **one** zero in $|z| < 1$. Equivalently, the equation $f(z) = z$ has exactly **one** solution in the open unit disc.

### PROOF COMPLETE
